title: Balanced sheaf dg tensor commutes with open extension by zero
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal S$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of associative unital dg $\mathcal S$-algebras. Use the sheafified balanced direct-sum total tensor, left-module signs and dg modules of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. A right module has $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any open inclusion and $j_!$ termwise extension by zero, with its dg action and canonical counit, as in [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus] (for right modules use the graded opposite algebra). Write $\mathcal A_U=\mathcal A|_U$.

For every right dg $\mathcal A_U$-module $L$ and left dg $\mathcal A$-module $N$, and every right dg $\mathcal A$-module $M$ and left dg $\mathcal A_U$-module $H$, the maps induced by the balanced tensor pairings give natural isomorphisms of complexes of $\mathcal S$-module sheaves
$$j_!L\otimes_{\mathcal A}N\simeq j_!(L\otimes_{\mathcal A_U}N|_U),\qquad M\otimes_{\mathcal A}j_!H\simeq j_!(M|_U\otimes_{\mathcal A_U}H).$$
On $U$ these maps identify the same pure tensors, and outside $U$ their stalks are the maps between zero objects. If $M$ additionally carries a commuting left action of a sheaf dg $\mathcal S$-algebra $\mathcal B$ (so it is a dg $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)$-bimodule), the second isomorphism is an isomorphism of left dg $\mathcal B$-modules with the action on the first tensor factor. The isomorphisms commute with open restriction, nested extension by zero and the counits to ambient tensors. The same assertions hold for graded modules and graded balanced tensors, with differentials omitted. No flatness, boundedness or commutativity of $\mathcal A$ is assumed; $U$ may be empty.

source.place: Tags 0FRB (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero) and 0FRX (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero-dg), and their left-module/opposite-algebra versions; retaining an additional commuting left dg action is the action-compatible form of these same canonical tensor identifications.

proof.text: Write $J=j_!$ on ordinary $\mathcal S_U$-modules. The degreewise underlying sheaves of the dg extension $j_!$ are these ordinary extensions by zero, by [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus]. Apply [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact] to the ringed space $(X,\mathcal S)$: $J$ is additive and left adjoint to open restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], it preserves all the direct sums and cokernels below, including their structure maps. The indexing sets $\{(p,q):p+q=n\}$ and $\{(r,s,t):r+s+t=n\}$ are small in the fixed universes; cokernels are coequalizers of a map and zero, and additivity preserves that zero. Thus the preservation theorem applies to these actual presentations, with no boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero); sdga Tag 0FRB (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero), last sentence of proof

proof.text: For ordinary module sheaves $F$ on $U$ and $G$ on $X$, apply [lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators] to the small site of opens of $X$ and its object $U$. Its slice is the open site of $U$, with the same restricted coefficient sheaf. It supplies the natural isomorphism $\psi_{F,G}:JF\otimes_{\mathcal S}G\to J(F\otimes_{\mathcal S_U}G|_U)$ and its inverse, with the specified rule $[f]\otimes g\mapsto[f\otimes g|_U]$. Brackets denote the sheafification images of extension-presheaf sections, not arbitrary global representatives. Iterating $\psi$, first on $JL^r\otimes\mathcal A^s$ and then tensoring with $N^t$, identifies $(JL^r\otimes\mathcal A^s)\otimes N^t$ with $J((L^r\otimes\mathcal A_U^s)\otimes N_U^t)$. Associating ordinary $\mathcal S$-tensors introduces no sign: both associations represent trilinear maps, by applying [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] twice. The inverse preserves the same ordered triples.

Use the balanced sheaf tensor of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. For any right graded $P$ and left graded $Q$, its degree $n$ is $\operatorname{coker}\rho_n$, where $\rho_n:\bigoplus_{r+s+t=n}(P^r\otimes_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A^s)\otimes_{\mathcal S}Q^t\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes_{\mathcal S}Q^q$ sends $p\otimes a\otimes q$ to $pa\otimes q-p\otimes aq$. Indeed maps from this cokernel are exactly families of bilinear pairings annihilating these relations, which is the defining sheafified balanced tensor universal property. For $P=JL,Q=N$, step 2 identifies both sums with $J$ of their counterparts on $U$. The two arrows of the balancing relation separately become $[la\otimes n]$ and $[l\otimes an]$, since extension actions extend the given action on $U$. Their difference is therefore $J\rho_{U,n}$. Step 1 identifies its cokernel with $J(\operatorname{coker}\rho_{U,n})$. These are inverse degreewise maps induced by the stated pairings, proving the first graded formula, with the identity on ordered pure tensors on $U$.

source.place: Tag 0FRB (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero), both displayed cokernel presentations; section-tensor-product

proof.text: Construct the ordinary second-slot comparison without commuting the algebra $\mathcal A$. Over the commutative base $\mathcal S$, the bilinear map $g\otimes f\mapsto f\otimes g$ has an inverse of the same form by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Compose this flip, $\psi_{F,G}$ of [lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators], and $J$ of the flip to get $\chi_{G,F}:G\otimes JF\cong J(G_U\otimes F)$, carrying $g\otimes[f]$ to $[g_U\otimes f]$. These are ordinary degreewise $\mathcal S$-tensors, so the auxiliary flips have no Koszul sign. Apply $\chi$ first to $\mathcal A^s\otimes JH^t$ and then to $M^r$ tensor that extension. On the triple relation the two arrows become $[ma\otimes h]$ and $[m\otimes ah]$. Applying step 1 to the cokernel presentation in step 3 gives $M\otimes_{\mathcal A}JH\cong J(M_U\otimes_{\mathcal A_U}H)$ as graded sheaves. At no point were a right and left $\mathcal A$-module interchanged.

source.place: Tag 0FRB (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero), same cokernel argument with extension in the second slot

proof.text:
For homogeneous $p,a,q$ with $|p|=r$ and $|a|=s$, let $\rho(p,a,q)=pa\otimes q-p\otimes aq$. The right and left Leibniz rules and the differential in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization] give
$$d\rho(p,a,q)=\rho(dp,a,q)+(-1)^r\rho(p,da,q)+(-1)^{r+s}\rho(p,a,dq).$$
Thus $d$ descends through the balanced relations. Its square on $p\otimes q$ is $d^2p\otimes q+((-1)^{r+1}+(-1)^r)dp\otimes dq+p\otimes d^2q=0$. For either graded comparison $\gamma$ of steps 3 and 4, applying $d\gamma$ or $\gamma d$ to an ordered generator gives exactly $[dp\otimes q+(-1)^rp\otimes dq]$, with the corresponding factor extended. Extension is degreewise and carries $d$ to $Jd$ by [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus]. Tensor, coproduct and cokernel universal properties then give equality of the sheaf maps. Hence both comparisons are chain isomorphisms: their degreewise inverses commute with $d$ by composing the chain-map identity with the inverses.

source.place: Tag 0FRX (lemma-tensor-with-extension-by-zero-dg), omitted differential verification; section-tensor-product-dg, displayed Leibniz computation

proof.text:
For the extra dg $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)$-bimodule structure on $M$, put $b\cdot(m\otimes h)=(bm)\otimes h$. The balancing relation is preserved because $(bm)a=b(ma)$, so its image is $bma\otimes h-bm\otimes ah$. Associativity and the unit follow from those of the left action on $M$. For $|b|=u,|m|=r$,
$$d((bm)\otimes h)=(db)m\otimes h+(-1)^ub(dm)\otimes h+(-1)^{u+r}bm\otimes dh=(db)\cdot(m\otimes h)+(-1)^ub\cdot d(m\otimes h).$$
The second projection comparison takes $(bm)\otimes[h]$ to $[(b|_U m)\otimes h]$, which is precisely the extended $\mathcal B$-action on its output. Therefore it and its inverse are $\mathcal B$-linear dg maps. Only a commuting left action is used, never graded commutativity of either algebra.

Naturality follows before taking cokernels: for maps $f$ of the first factor and $g$ of the second, either composite sends an ordered generator to $[f(p)\otimes g(q)]$. This is also the naturality of the ordinary comparisons in [lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators]. The induced maps on sums and cokernels are consequently natural, and so are their inverses. On $U$, the unit identification of [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus] identifies each extension with the original sheaf and both projection maps with the identity on pure tensors; hence with the identity sheaf map by the tensor and quotient universal properties. Outside $U$, each right-hand complex is termwise an extension by zero, so has zero stalk in every degree by that same calculus. The degreewise isomorphisms already proved force the left-hand stalks to be zero too. The stalk maps are therefore the unique maps between zero objects. This argument requires no theorem commuting noncommutative balanced dg tensor with stalks.

source.place: Tags 0FRB and 0FRX, functoriality and normalization of the displayed identifications

proof.text: Let $k:V\hookrightarrow X$, $T=U\cap V$, and $j':T\hookrightarrow V$. On the open sites the inclusion of opens of $V$ is continuous and cocontinuous: a covering of an open contained in $V$ consists of opens still contained in $V$, with the identical union. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction] identifies restriction of each sheafified tensor presentation with the sheafification of its restricted presentation, preserving the original unit sections. The direct-sum and balanced-quotient presheaf formulas are the same on every open of $V$, so this gives the required restriction identifications for both tensors. Use also $k^*j_!\cong j'_!(-|_T)$ from [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus]. After these identifications, restricting either projection map gives the projection for $j'$, since both send the original ordered pair to that same pair on $T$. The unit-section equality criterion in the sheafification-restriction node gives equality of the resulting sheaf maps. Differential compatibility was checked in step 5.

source.place: Tag 04B8 (lemma-almost-cocontinuous-sheafification); sdga Tags 0FRB and 0FRX, restriction of the explicit tensor maps

proof.text:
For nested opens $W\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, compare the projection for $ji$ with the composite of the two projections and the compositor $(ji)_!\cong j_!i_!$ from [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus]. By steps 3 and 4, the source is degreewise an extension from $W$. The ordinary adjunction of [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact] implies that two maps from this source agree if their restrictions to $W$, composed with the unit, agree. Both composites there are the identity on the same ordered pure tensor, including the unit-normalized compositor. Hence they agree in every degree. This also proves coherence for further nested opens. For an ambient right module $P$ and left module $Q$, writing $\varepsilon$ for the extension counit, the two counit compatibilities are
$$\varepsilon_{P\otimes_{\mathcal A}Q}\gamma_1=\varepsilon_P\otimes1_Q,\qquad \varepsilon_{P\otimes_{\mathcal A}Q}\gamma_2=1_P\otimes\varepsilon_Q,$$
where $\gamma_1$ is evaluated at $(P|_U,Q)$ and $\gamma_2$ at $(P,Q|_U)$. Each source is degreewise an extension from $U$ by the formulas proved above. Under the ordinary adjunction both sides restrict to $p\otimes q\mapsto p\otimes q$, since the counits restrict to the identity. Thus these are equalities of actual chain maps. Naturality gives the versions with a supplied map to an ambient factor.

source.place: Tags 0FRB and 0FRX, canonical pairing refinements; sites-modules Tag 03DI, uniqueness under the open adjunction

proof.text: Steps 1--4 and 7--9 use only graded components, actions, sheaf maps and universal properties; deleting the differentials gives the asserted graded versions with the same normalizations and coherences. The construction never asks tensor to preserve a kernel or a quasi-isomorphism: only extension of sums and cokernels is used. It therefore imposes no flatness, boundedness or commutativity hypothesis on $\mathcal A$. For $U=\varnothing$, extension by zero is zero degreewise by [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-calculus], so all displayed maps are the unique isomorphisms of zero complexes. For $U=X$ the maps are identities, as their pure-tensor formulas show.
